summary: Global equity markets are attempting back-to-back gains amid cautious optimism, with investors leaning on corporate earnings as the primary catalyst to sustain the broader bull market, while Jim Cramer's highlighted "magic elixir" points to a mix of momentum and selective risk appetite driving Tuesday's session. On the macro front, geopolitical tensions are a dominant theme, with Iran conditioning diplomatic engagement on unmet demands, UK authorities arresting individuals linked to Iranian intelligence, and Britain committing to defensive air missions over Saudi Arabia, all signaling a deteriorating Middle East security environment. At the sector and stock level, Netflix is drawing renewed trader interest amid signs its prolonged volatility may be stabilizing, Apple secured a win as Qnity captures iPhone business, Anthropic is in advanced talks with Nscale over a multibillion-dollar AI infrastructure deal, and Novo Nordisk's next-generation obesity drug posted impressive 25% weight loss data in women, lifting sentiment around the healthcare space. The primary risk factors investors are monitoring include escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and airports — which sent most Gulf bourses into the red — ongoing conflict in Gaza, and rising far-right political momentum in Israel ahead of elections, all of which threaten to amplify energy price volatility and regional instability. In the near term, the short-term outlook hinges on whether earnings results, including a closely watched SpaceX report after the bell, can provide sufficient fundamental support to push the S&P 500 through its key technical resistance level and extend the rally meaningfully.
